answer: Rain on a window makes a patter whose density and spectral shape depend on the glass, the frame, and the storm outside, so a phone can prove its place by matching a short rain recording against a local weather microphone in the same minutes. A farm indoors hears no rain at all, and downloading a rain sample fails because the live storm's gusts and lulls never repeat exactly. The pigment of a grey sky says nothing without the sound, a jade of wet leaves adds its own patter, and the ridge of a roofline shapes the drops in a pattern only a real window can witness.
